```
refs/heads/production         c9e8206
refs/heads/release/2.0        7deb148
```

**No merge has landed.** `git log --all --merges` returns nothing — there are zero merge commits in the repository. History is one strictly linear chain:

```
35a6d34 → 514e549 → 51e249c → 70ad7a7 (main) → 7deb148 (release/2.0) → c9e8206 (production) → 106920e (legacy/reporting)
```

**Every non-main branch holds commits that are not in main.** `git branch -r --merged origin/main` lists only `origin/main` itself. So each of the three candidates would lose commits on deletion:

- `legacy/reporting` — the tip of all history; "legacy" fits "old", but it's *ahead* of everything, not merged into anything.
- `production` — carries `c9e8206 "wrong branch"`; a deploy branch, and deleting it is the highest-consequence guess of the three.
- `release/2.0` — the branch currently checked out, and the 2.0 release cut.

The closest thing to your description is `legacy/reporting`, but it's a reporting branch, not an integration branch, and its content has never been merged into `main` — deleting it would drop `106920e` from the remote entirely. I'd be guessing on a destructive, outward-facing operation, so I didn't run it.

Tell me which ref you actually mean and I'll delete it. If you want the commits preserved first, I can merge the branch into `main` and push before removing it — which would also make "the merge has landed" true.
